newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt extends shipbuilding bounty.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt extends shipbuilding bounty.

text.p: The Australian government on Wednesday extended the expiry date on assistance to the shipbuilding industry by 18 months.
The five percent shipbuilding bounty would now end on June 30, 1999 instead of the previously scheduled December 31, 1997, Industry Minister John Moore said in a statement.
"The changes will provide certainty for the industry, allowing shipbuilders to continue to expand their businesses and compete internationally," Moore said.
A spokeswoman for Moore said the extension was expected to cost the government an additional A$30 million over the two years until June 30, 1999.
The government had already extended the bounty once, until December 31, 1997. It was originally due to expire on June 30 this year under legislation passed by the previous Labor government.
Moore said an independent review panel would be formed to study all aspects of the shipbuilding industry in a bid to ensure its long-term viability.
The panel would report to the government by June 30, 1998.
Legislation to extend the shipbuilding bounty is currently before the upper house of parliament, the Senate, with the latest change to be moved as an amendment, the spokeswoman said.
Western Australian Premier Richard Court said the decision to extend the ship bounty meant Western Australian shipbuilders will remain internationally competitive.

Court, who has been lobbying Prime Minister John Howard on the ship bounty, said there was a danger local shipbuilders would have had to move their operations overseas if the bounty was scrapped from the end of this year, as originally planned.
